From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmehealth.com>, Tom Davenport <tom.davenport@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: AcmeHealth — Private VPC dataflow & PII handling (post-call follow-up)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the security and infra team. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize the immediate follow-ups and confirm a few details so our security review and PoC planning can move forward quickly.

Key items we discussed (and what we need to confirm):
1) PII scope and retention
   - You indicated that AcmeHealth will send patient identifiers and limited PHI to Redwood inside prompt payloads for inference.
   - Please confirm if any of the payloads will include long-term patient histories or only near-term encounter context.
   - Confirmation needed: desired retention policy on Redwood side (options: ephemeral/no-retention, 30d, 90d) and any legal/regulatory constraints.

2) Logging and access controls
   - We proposed redact-on-ingest + KMS-managed keying for any persisted logs.
   - Please confirm the list of roles who need access to logs and whether you require audit log forwarding to your SIEM.

3) Private/VPC deployment & network boundaries
   - Deployment model: Private VPC (Redwood-managed control plane, customer-managed VPC peering) vs. fully on-prem/air-gapped.
   - For the VPC model, we need your network CIDR for peering and the egress requirements (internet egress blocked vs. allowed to our update endpoints).
   - If on-prem/air-gapped is required, please note additional lead time for packaging and HSM/KMS integrations.

4) Egress controls and allowed destinations
   - We support explicit allowlists for outbound traffic from the inference cluster.
   - Confirm whether you require zero egress (forbid all internet) or allow specific domains (e.g., redwood-updates.redwood.ai, pacemaker-registry.redwood.ai).

Attachments we can share today:
- SOC2-snapshot.pdf (internal SOC2 summary)
- Example network diagram for Private VPC deployment (attached)

Next steps / asks from AcmeHealth:
- Quick answers to items 1-4 above so we can finalize the security questionnaire and scope the PoC (recommended: ephemeral retention, KMS with customer-managed keys).
- Please attach your network diagram if you have one with VPC CIDRs and any transit gateways.
- If useful, propose 30-45 minute follow-up slot next week for Neha (security) and Dev (infra) to run a deeper dataflow review.

If I missed anything from the call, shout — thanks again.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

--

Subject: Re: AcmeHealth — Private VPC dataflow & PII handling (post-call follow-up)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers inline below and attached our network diagram.

1) PII scope and retention
   - We will be sending identifiers + short notes (patient id, recent encounter context, medication list). No full longitudinal records in this initial PoC.
   - Retention: we prefer ephemeral/no-retention for inference payloads; if Redwood requires short-term logs for debugging, limit to 7 days and we require automatic redaction of direct identifiers.

2) Logging and access controls
   - Access: only AcmeHealth Security (security@acmehealth.com) and a named Redwood support account should be able to request logs.
   - We will want audit log forwarding to our Splunk instance; Tom will share the ingestion endpoint.

3) Private/VPC deployment & network boundaries
   - We'll start with Private VPC (peered). CIDR for peering: 10.20.0.0/16.
   - Egress: our default posture is deny-all outbound except explicit allowlist. We will allow specific Redwood update endpoints listed below.
   - On-prem/air-gap: not required for PoC, but possible for later-stage procurement.

4) Egress controls and allowed destinations
   - Zero egress by default; allowlist to include:
     * updates.redwood.ai (for security patch checks)
     * registry.redwood.ai (model artifact pull, TLS only)
   - We'll provide fully-qualified domains and IP ranges next week.

Attachments: acme_network_diagram_v2.png

Next steps:
- Tom will drop the Splunk forwarding endpoint and list of allowed domains by Monday.
- We can do a technical review with Neha + Dev on Tuesday 3/2 at 10:00 PT if that works (Tom & Sarah to confirm).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sarah
Sr. Security Engineer | AcmeHealth

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the quick responses and the updated network diagram — received and attached to our ticket. Quick confirmation and next steps from our side: 

- Ephemeral retention + 7-day debug logs with automatic identifier redaction: we can support this. For KMS, we recommend customer-managed keys; can your infosec team confirm they can provide an AWS KMS ARN for the PoC?
- Audit log forwarding to Splunk: Dev — can you confirm the supported log forwarder formats and any firewall rules we need to set on our side?
- VPC peering: 10.20.0.0/16 noted. We'll prepare a peering checklist and the minimal inbound CIDRs for the inference cluster.
- Egress allowlist: we will support allowlisting by FQDN and/or IPs. For the PoC we can allow updates.redwood.ai and registry.redwood.ai; long-term we can provide a stable set of IP ranges.

Proposed timeline:
- Tue 3/2 10:00 PT: technical review call (Neha + Dev + Tom + Sarah) — confirm if this works.
- By Wed 3/3: Redwood will share a short security questionnaire with answers for Acme to review.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite once Tom confirms the Splunk endpoint.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Marissa
